overview: Both are lipids built from glycerol and fatty acids, but they differ by one substitution that changes their role entirely.
genZNote: Triglyceride: glycerol with three fatty tails, built for storage. Phospholipid: swap one tail for a phosphate head, and now it can build membranes.

aspects.label: Structure
aspects.valueA: Glycerol backbone bonded to three fatty acid chains.
aspects.valueB: Glycerol backbone bonded to two fatty acid chains and one phosphate group.

aspects.label: Polarity
aspects.valueB: Amphipathic — has a hydrophilic phosphate head and hydrophobic fatty acid tails.

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueB: Forms the structural bilayer of all cell membranes.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Phospholipids' amphipathic nature is exactly why they spontaneously form the bilayer structure of cell membranes in water.
overlay.memoryTrick: Tri = three fatty tails, storage. Phospho = phosphate head added, membrane building.
overlay.commonMisconception: Triglycerides cannot form stable membranes in water — their lack of a polar head group means they simply clump together as fat droplets.
